newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agreement on modified cotton plan seen Friday.
newsitem.headline: EU agreement on modified cotton plan seen Friday.

text.p: The European Union is likely to agree on Friday a modified plan for definitive anti-dumping duties on cotton imports from China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Turkey and Pakistan, a European Commission spokesman said on Thursday.

He said after a second meeting of EU ambassadors on Thursday that there was "quite a strong likelihood" that national capitals would now agree to the Commission's modified proposal for duties on unbleached cotton fabric imports from the countries named.
Diplomats said earlier on Thursday that nine of the EU's 15 countries had rejected the proposal, making it likely the plan would lapse come the May 20 expiry date for provisional duties.
But a Commission offer to review the duties after one year appeared to have swung three countries -- Austria, Germany and Luxembourg -- behind the six who originally backed the plan.
Belgium, Greece, Spain, France, Italy and Portugal supported the proposal earlier on Thursday, two countries shy of the simple majority needed to impose final duties.

"The Commission saw how finely balanced the thing was," the spokesman said in reference both to EU countries' positions and to the conflicting positions on duties of EU cotton producers and cotton finishers.
"The best thing for the Commission to do was to modify the proposal so that a full review can take place within the shortest possible time -- That is to say one year," he added.

The spokesman said duties remained unchanged from provisional ones, meaning the Chinese-origin imports face 18.9 percent duties, those from Egypt 13 percent, India 17.2 percent, Indonesia 14.5 percent, Pakistan 22.9 percent and Turkey 17.5 percent.
Companies which have cooperated with EU dumping officials' inquiries generally face reduced rates.
The Commission imposed provisional duties against grey cotton fabrics from the six named countries last November, setting in train the further review period expiring on May 20.
One diplomat said capitals would have to make their positions clear by the end of Friday so as to allow legal texts to be finalised for May 20.
